narrative.overview:
The public site belongs to the netsmartz.com family: a white page with full-width deep navy bands, Netsmartz orange, and bold, tightly tracked Inter. The page shows a voice agent at work before it sells one. The signature is a lit orange orb on navy with status chips around it, and a sample call that plays into a captured-fields panel. Everything else stays quiet so that orange always means "do this" or "this is live".

The rhythm alternates white sections with navy bands (hero, call demo, Netsmartz proof, close, footer) and uses a quiet grey section for use cases. Layouts are asymmetric 12-column splits. Copy sits in a 5-6 column side and the working object (orb, transcript, list) fills the other side. Depth is soft and low-contrast. Corners are generous on containers and tighter on controls.

Light is the default theme. The public site opens light unless the visitor has saved a theme choice. A dark theme flips the ground to navy, and navy bands then go one step deeper.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, deep navy bands, one orange accent reserved for actions and live signal.
Inter only, bold (700) with negative tracking on headings.
8px buttons with navy text on orange.
Hairline (#E5E7EB) structure, soft navy-tinted shadows, an orange-tinted lift on hover.
An orange radial light lives only around the orb.
Motion is gentle and fully disabled under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange is reserved for actions and live signal. Icon tiles are neutral ink on the quiet surface. The one exception is the Most popular agent, whose tile and badge are solid orange. Decorative orange icons, orange section fills and orange headings are not part of this system.

rules.name: The Navy Text Rule
rules.body: Anything set on an orange fill is navy #0B1220, never white.

rules.name: The Band Flip Rule
rules.body: A navy band re-points the neutral tokens (ink, muted, surface, line, orange-ink, focus) instead of restyling components. Primitives dropped into a band must read correctly without per-component overrides.

rules.name: The Heavy-and-Tight Rule
rules.body: Every heading is weight 700 with negative tracking. No light or thin display weights.

rules.name: The Orb Light Rule
rules.body: Orange radial light appears only around the orb. The orb carries its own radial halo at every size. The wider section-level hero glow (radial at 80% / 42%) renders only in the two-column layout (lg and up). When stacked, the orb's own glow is enough. Cards may show a faint pointer-following orange sheen on hover, but no other section gets an orange glow.

dos: Do set every label on orange in navy #0B1220.
Do keep orange to actions (buttons, active states, links in orange-ink) and live signal (bars, pulse, booked states).
Do use neutral ink icon tiles, and reserve the solid orange tile for the Most popular agent.
Do alternate white sections with full-width deep navy bands, and let the band flip re-point tokens.
Do set headings in Inter 700 with negative tracking (-0.03em to -0.035em).
Do use 8px button corners, 16px card corners and #E5E7EB hairlines.
Do label any illustrative conversation or call visual as a sample.
Do honour reduced motion: a still orb, the full transcript, and no drift, pulse or tilt.
donts: Don't put white text on #FE7725, because it fails AA.
Don't use raw #FE7725 for text on white. Use orange-ink #B4500F (or #FF9555 on navy).
Don't place orange radial light anywhere except around the orb, and don't show the section-level hero glow outside the two-column layout.
Don't tint icon tiles orange for decoration.
Don't introduce a second typeface. Inter is a confirmed brand commitment.
Don't use hard, offset or high-contrast shadows. Depth stays soft and navy-tinted.
Don't restyle the signed-in workspace from these tokens. It keeps its own :root set.
